explanations: Inside the nested loop over each member's grants, `await this.repo.grantorEmail(g.grantedBy)` issues one users query per role grant, one after another. Members, grants and logins are batched, but grantor emails are N+1: an org with 2,000 members and 5 grants each makes about 10,000 sequential queries, and the same few admins are looked up over and over. The distinct grantedBy ids should be collected and resolved with a single `id = ANY($1)` query.

lastLoginsForUsers filters `outcome = 'success'`, so the failed login is ignored and lastLogin is 120 days ago. That is before the 90-day cutoff, so stale is true. lastLogin is not null because a successful login exists.

grantsForUsers has `g.org_id = $1`, so only this org's grants appear. lastLoginsForUsers filters only by user_id, so logins are counted regardless of org. Roles are not global and status does not affect which grants load.

The injected clock is used only to compute the 90-day cutoff, which makes the stale logic testable with a fixed time. It does no time-zone conversion, it is called once rather than for performance, and it is unrelated to how Postgres returns timestamps.
